subject: RFP: Offline orchestration & operator compatibility for private deployments
messages:
From: Dr. Emily Han <e.han@novamed.io>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novamed.io, alan.brooks@secureinfra.io
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: offline orchestration & operator compatibility for private deployments

Hi Sofia / Jonas,

Thanks for taking our initial call last week. As we finalize the RFP packet for NovaMed's private deployment evaluation, there are three areas we need concrete answers and evidence for before we advance the shortlist:

1) Operator access and separation: a clear matrix of operator roles, least-privilege boundaries, and how operator activity is audited in completely offline (air-gapped) installs.
2) Orchestration compatibility: how Redwood's runtime integrates with customer orchestration (k8s variants, bare-metal job schedulers) in environments with no egress, and the expected manual steps for upgrades.
3) KMS and key bootstrap: pattern for seeding customer KMS/HSM with keys, rotation procedures in an isolated network, and ability to attest key provenance for audits.

We'd like short written responses plus any artifacts (runbooks, diagrams, role matrix). Can you return this by EOD Thursday Pacific (2027-04-01)? Procurement will include Alan from our security consultants on any technical follow-ups.

Best,
Emily Han
Director, Engineering Operations
NovaMed Health

[attachment: RFP-Questionnaire-NovaMed.pdf (application/pdf)]

Sofia / Irene / Marissa —

Summarizing what I'll provide and what I need from you by Wednesday (tomorrow):

What I'll produce:
- KMS network diagram (high level) + attestation text describing signing/rotation sequence (kms-network-diagram.png)
- Upgrade playbook (offline-safe steps, preflight checks, operator pause window)

What I need from Irene:
- Audit event list mapping (operator action -> event id -> retention location). We should make sure field names line up with NovaMed's SOC2 evidence columns.
What I need from Marissa:
- Operator-access-matrix.xlsx: role names, allowed consoles/CLIs, jump-host pattern, 3rd-party vendor operator rules, and sample revoke workflow.

Notes on compatibility: Redwood's runtime supports the following patterns in offline installs:
- k8s (v1.22+): admission webhook disabled mode with manual configmap sync for model assets
- kubeadm & RKE: supported; we add a small operator shim that runs as a static pod for KV cache persistence
- Bare-metal schedulers: manual service wrapper + systemd unit; documented in the playbook

I'll assemble everything into a single archive and upload to our restricted Drive link. Expect the package plus a one-page executive summary.

Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Architect

Subject: Re: RFP: offline orchestration & operator compatibility for private deployments

Emily / Alan / Procurement team —

Attached is our response package for NMH-RFP-2027-042. Contents and highlights below:

Attachments (uploaded and attached):
- operator-access-matrix.xlsx — role definitions, least-privilege mappings, example revoke flow (column headers match typical SOC2 evidence fields).
- upgrade-checklist.pdf — step-by-step offline upgrade playbook including preflight checks, operator pause commands, rollback triggers and minutes-to-operator-impact estimates.
- kms-network-diagram.png — key bootstrap and rotation flow for HSM-backed KMS; includes offline key import steps and recommended attestation log sequence.

Key clarifications (short):
1) Operator separation & audit: our recommended pattern uses a three-tier operator model (Admin, Operator, ReadOnly) with jump-hosting for any write operations. All operator actions are recorded locally to immutable append-only logs and exported as signed bundles when a walled-garden export is approved. We include the event ID mapping and a sample signed export proof.

2) Orchestration integration: for fully offline clusters we support a manual sync model for model assets (rsync over mounted media or controlled airgap push). The runtime runs as standard containers; we provide a static-pod helper for runtime persistence where kubelet-only environments exist. Upgrades require an operator-controlled maintenance window; checklist describes health checks to run.

3) KMS bootstrap & attestation: we support customers using KMS/HSM (PKCS#11) or cloud KMS adapters in Bring-Your-Own-Key mode. For offline HSMs we document a physical key import flow and an attestation sequence involving signed manifests and a notarized rotation ledger.

Next steps we propose:
- Technical review call (60 min) with Alan and NovaMed security to walk artifacts: Tue 2027-04-06 10:00 PT or Wed 2027-04-07 14:00 PT. Please confirm preferred time.
- If Alan provides any required evidence template (spreadsheet columns or signed attestation form), we'll conform artifacts and resubmit within 48 hours of receipt.

Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/secure/NMH-RFP-2027 (restricted link)

Thanks — we're happy to augment the package with any additional evidence you need for audits.

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
